scope_notes: Approximately two-hour browser-based introduction to optimization in MATLAB, teaching optimization variables, objectives, constraints and solving practical optimization problems with automated feedback.
prerequisites: Basic MATLAB familiarity is helpful; no advanced optimization prerequisite
required_resources: Modern browser; MATLAB Online environment is provided for the course and no paid product license is required

component_evidence.pedagogy: Concepts are introduced directly inside an interactive MATLAB environment and tied to realistic optimization problems rather than taught as passive exposition.
component_evidence.depth: The course is intentionally compact and introduces practical optimization workflow rather than developing optimization theory in depth.
component_evidence.practice: Hands-on browser exercises, automated checks and instant feedback create unusually strong practice for a two-hour course.
component_evidence.materials: MathWorks integrates explanation, executable examples, coding exercises and progress tracking in one environment.
component_evidence.currency: Optimization Onramp remains part of MathWorks' current 2026 Onramp catalogue and uses the live MATLAB Online environment.
component_evidence.expertise: MathWorks has direct expertise in numerical optimization, MATLAB and technical computing education.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course is free for everyone, browser-based, requires no separate product license and includes a shareable completion certificate.

recommendation_rationale: Excellent practical optimization onboarding with very strong interactive feedback, but the two-hour scope and MATLAB-specific workflow keep it below full university optimization courses as a general recommendation.

academic_credits: No academic credit for independent OCW learners
scope_notes: Complete undergraduate complex-analysis course covering complex algebra and geometry, analytic functions, contour integration, Cauchy's theorem and formula, harmonic functions, conformal mappings, argument principle, Laplace transforms and related applications, with lecture/problem-solving notes, recitations, nine problem sets and exams with solutions.
prerequisites: Single-variable calculus and multivariable-calculus maturity are expected
required_resources: General-purpose computer/browser; complete course materials are downloadable and no paid software is required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course combines conceptual lecture notes with problem-solving notes and recitations, supporting both theory and application rather than relying on lectures alone.
component_evidence.depth: A full semester develops core undergraduate complex analysis through contour methods, conformal mapping and applications at substantial mathematical depth.
component_evidence.practice: Nine problem sets with complete solutions, recitation exercises and multiple practice/exam resources provide sustained proof and computation practice.
component_evidence.materials: OCW exposes a complete package of lecture notes, problem-solving notes, recitations, assignments, exams and solutions suitable for independent study.
component_evidence.currency: Complex-analysis foundations are highly stable; the Spring 2018 date creates essentially no conceptual obsolescence for the syllabus.
component_evidence.expertise: MIT mathematics faculty and course staff provide strong subject expertise in analysis and applied mathematics.
component_evidence.accessibility: All materials are openly downloadable, but the calculus prerequisites and proof-oriented mathematical maturity create meaningful entry friction.

recommendation_rationale: An exceptionally complete free complex-analysis course with strong solution-backed practice. Its only substantial recommendation constraint is prerequisite difficulty, not age.

academic_credits: No academic credit for independent OCW learners
scope_notes: Complete undergraduate number-theory course covering divisibility, Euclidean algorithm, primes, congruences, Chinese remainder theorem, cryptographic applications, primitive roots, quadratic residues and reciprocity, with lecture notes, nine problem sets and exam/practice materials with solutions.
prerequisites: Mathematical maturity and comfort with proof are expected; no advanced number-theory prerequisite
required_resources: General-purpose computer/browser; downloadable course package and no paid software required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course develops classical number theory through a sequence of definitions, theorems, proofs and computational applications such as RSA.
component_evidence.depth: A full undergraduate semester reaches from elementary divisibility through quadratic reciprocity and core algebraic-number-theory ideas.
component_evidence.practice: Nine problem sets with solutions plus midterm/final practice problems and solutions provide strong proof-oriented practice.
component_evidence.materials: Lecture notes, assignments, solutions, exam guidelines and practice examinations form a coherent independent-study package.
component_evidence.currency: The underlying mathematics is highly stable; the 2012 date is not a meaningful subject-currentness defect.
component_evidence.expertise: MIT mathematics faculty provide strong expertise in number theory and proof-based undergraduate mathematics.
component_evidence.accessibility: Everything is free and downloadable, but proof maturity and the abstract nature of the subject limit beginner accessibility.

recommendation_rationale: A rigorous, complete free number-theory course with excellent problem-set support. Recommendation is limited mainly by proof prerequisites and specialist scope.
